title: US Workers Name AI Skills as 'Career Currency'
paragraphs: As AI tools become more common in the workplace, knowing how to use them could soon be an important addition to your resume.
A survey by Talker Research asked 2,000 US adults how they feel about AI and employment.
More than half — 57% — said they think certifications in AI know-how are becoming a new kind of "career currency," meaning something that gives you an advantage in the workplace.

Younger survey participants are even more likely to see AI certification as important for career growth. Sixty-five percent of millennials — born between 1981 and 1996 — said it's valuable, as did 64% of Gen Z, born between 1997 and 2008.
But even if people think AI skills are good to have, perceptions of its use at work tend to be a little less positive.

In the survey, a little less than half of all Americans had a favorable opinion of AI in the workplace. This rose to 58% among Gen Z and 56% for millennials, but stayed below the number of respondents in these groups who felt AI certification offered career currency.
The survey also found that many workers aren't sure how well they can use AI tools at work, with 48% not feeling qualified to do so.

However, half of respondents also think that in just six months, every new hire will need to know how to use AI effectively in the workplace. And whether they already use it or not, two-thirds of employed survey respondents said they expect AI to have an impact on their career path within the next year.
Sixty-two percent of employed respondents also said they would use AI more often at work if they were more confident in its effectiveness, were encouraged to use it, or if they were trained to do so.
